summary:
MARY
We developed a software framework specifically designed for long-duration spaceflight missions to evaluate real-time physiological monitoring data uploaded throughout the expedition, comparing it against baseline metrics delivered from previous missions. Because prolonged exposure to microgravity significantly elevates ocular risks, our primary focus is on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a high-risk and prevalent condition among astronauts. The platform processes telemetry acquired from biomedical hardware, including smart biometric garments, finger arterial tonometers, and the Bio-Monitor system. Furthermore, it integrates longitudinal health tracking and comprehensive patient histories, while deploying automated, strict clinical protocols for both routine procedures and medical emergencies. On the ground, the telemetry link between Mission Control and the spacecraft operates seamlessly.
details:
Our software, M.O.G.A. (Medical Ocular & General Attention), evaluates physiological metrics and clinical test results collected from astronauts at different stages of the rout. It is specifically designed for long-duration, deep-space missions, which is why our primary focus is on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)—a condition with an alarming frequency-to-risk ratio that poses a latent, high-risk threat during prolonged exposure to microgravity, unlike short-duration flights.

The application was engineered to operate autonomously during emergencies. If an accident occurs or a preventive procedure is required, the corresponding clinical protocol is automatically displayed on screen as soon as the software detects anomalies or injuries.

M.O.G.A. interfaces via sensors with specialized biomedical hardware—such as Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) scanners, ocular ultrasound systems, and smart biometric garments, among other integrated devices. The system collects raw telemetry and translates it into standard clinical parameters, guiding the crew through routine health checks and medical care. Overall, it is a practical, automated platform that eliminates manual data entry and uploading, making space medicine practices faster and more streamlined. It collects the medical records for next missions

To develop this medical tool, we utilized the AI models Claude and Gemini within Visual Studio Code, following extensive research into aerospace medical hardware. While the dataset currently displayed on the platform serves as a simulation, the system is designed to integrate with the following onboard medical equipment:

· Diagnostic & Imaging: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) scanner, multifunctional portable ultrasound (with tablet interface), ocular ultrasound, handheld tonometer, and digital ophthalmoscope/otoscope (with cobalt blue light), Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) scanners, ocular ultrasound systems

· Cardiopulmonary & Vital Signs Monitoring: Multiparameter patient monitor, pulse oximeter, automatic non-invasive blood pressure (NIBP) monitor, 12-lead electrocardiograph (ECG) with Holter monitor, smart biometric garments, biometric patches, and digital portable spirometer, and smart biometric garments

· Laboratory & Radiation Analysis: Portable blood chemistry and blood gas analyzer (i-STAT type), portable hematology analyzer, compact immunoassay analyzer, urinalysis test strips with refractometer/urinary iodine analyzer, and active personal radiation dosimeters,

· Emergency, Resuscitation & Surgical Support: Automated External Defibrillator (AED) with manual mode and transcutaneous pacing, portable transport mechanical ventilator with 100% oxygen concentrator/tanks, portable closed-suction aspirator, video laryngoscope and airway kit, compact intravenous (IV) infusion pump (or pressurized bags), medical stretcher with body restraint system, transparent surgical canopy with integrated suction, minor surgery and trauma instrument kit, sealed continuous ocular irrigation goggles, emergency breathing apparatus (PBA) masks with HEPA filters, and a system-classified pharmacological kit.
